description_good_justification: The README opens with what the app is and the problem it solves: https://github.com/dota2modmanager/dota2-mod-manager/blob/main/README.md
interact_justification: The README links the download, the issue tracker and CONTRIBUTING.md: https://github.com/dota2modmanager/dota2-mod-manager/blob/main/README.md
contribution_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md describes the pull request flow, the required checks and the rule that a fix arrives with a test: https://github.com/dota2modmanager/dota2-mod-manager/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states what a change has to carry: npm run verify, a test or a No-Test-Because line, and the style the repository keeps: https://github.com/dota2modmanager/dota2-mod-manager/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
floss_license_justification: GPL-3.0-or-later (NOTICE says: version 3 of the License, or any later version): https://github.com/dota2modmanager/dota2-mod-manager/blob/main/NOTICE
floss_license_osi_justification: GPL-3.0 is approved by the Open Source Initiative.
documentation_basics_justification: Guides on the project site (https://dota2modmanager.com/docs/) and the README.
documentation_interface_justification: The app is a desktop program. Its external interfaces are documented in three places: the window itself with screenshots on the site, the d2mm:// link format and the settings file in ARCHITECTURE.md, and every exported function of every module in docs/API.md, which is generated from the source and fails CI when it drifts: https://github.com/dota2modmanager/dota2-mod-manager/blob/main/docs/API.md
sites_https_justification: github.com, dota2modmanager.com and cdn.dota2modmanager.com are HTTPS only.
discussion_justification: GitHub Issues and Discussions, plus the project Discord: https://github.com/dota2modmanager/dota2-mod-manager/issues
english_justification: Every document in the repository is in English; README.ru.md and CHANGELOG.ru.md are twins for Russian users. Issues are answered in English.
maintained_justification: Released 30 times since July 2026, with commits most days: https://github.com/dota2modmanager/dota2-mod-manager/commits/main
repo_track_justification: git records what changed, who changed it and when, for every commit in the repository.
repo_interim_justification: Every change lands on main through a pull request between releases, so the repository carries the work rather than only the tags.
repo_distributed_justification: git, hosted on GitHub, and every clone carries the whole history.
version_unique_justification: Each release is a vX.Y.Z tag and the same version in package.json: https://github.com/dota2modmanager/dota2-mod-manager/releases
version_semver_justification: Semantic Versioning: features raise the minor, fixes the patch, as CONTRIBUTING.md states.
version_tags_justification: Pushing the git tag is what starts a release: https://github.com/dota2modmanager/dota2-mod-manager/blob/main/RELEASING.md
release_notes_justification: CHANGELOG.md holds a section per version, and the release workflow puts that section on the GitHub release: https://github.com/dota2modmanager/dota2-mod-manager/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
release_notes_vulns_justification: No vulnerability has been reported in this project own code. When an advisory in a dependency touched the app, the notes said so: the 2.6.11 section describes the adm-zip path traversal advisory and explains that the app never lets that library write to disk, so no installed mod could have used it.
report_process_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md, "Reporting a bug", and issue templates: https://github.com/dota2modmanager/dota2-mod-manager/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
report_responses_justification: Every issue opened so far has an answer from the maintainer. CONTRIBUTING.md promises a first reply within 72 hours, and a daily job (tools/radar.mjs) measures the project against that promise and messages the maintainer when something is overdue.
enhancement_responses_justification: Enhancement requests are answered, and the ones taken up are labelled and linked to the change that implemented them.
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: GitHub private vulnerability reporting is enabled, and SECURITY.md sends reporters there: https://github.com/dota2modmanager/dota2-mod-manager/blob/main/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability report has been received. SECURITY.md promises a first reply within 48 hours, and the daily job watches that promise.
build_justification: npm ci, then npm run dist (electron-builder). CI builds the installer, the portable build and the AppImage for every release: https://github.com/dota2modmanager/dota2-mod-manager/blob/main/.github/workflows/release.yml
build_floss_tools_justification: Node.js, npm and electron-builder are FLOSS.
test_justification: npm test: more than 80 test files on node:test, released under the project own licence: https://github.com/dota2modmanager/dota2-mod-manager/tree/main/test
test_invocation_justification: npm test, which is what CI runs as well.
test_most_justification: Coverage is measured on every run and held two ways: an aggregate floor of 90% of lines in the gate, and each file own number per platform in .github/coverage-baseline.json, which a run below them fails. Measured today it is about 93% of lines and 87% of branches, with the modules that write into the player game folder above 85%.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: The suite runs on Linux and on Windows for every push and every pull request: https://github.com/dota2modmanager/dota2-mod-manager/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states that a fix arrives with a test, or with a No-Test-Because line saying why none is possible. A required check on every pull request ("A fix brings its test") enforces it against the diff.
tests_are_added_justification: The required check refuses a fix with no test and no stated reason, so the policy holds on every merged pull request. Beyond that, .github/mutants.json holds deliberate breakages of the promises the tests guard, and a weekly run breaks each one to check the suite notices.
tests_documented_added_justification: The policy is in CONTRIBUTING.md, in the section on what a good pull request looks like: https://github.com/dota2modmanager/dota2-mod-manager/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
warnings_justification: ESLint for code that cannot run, and tsc --checkJs over the JSDoc: https://github.com/dota2modmanager/dota2-mod-manager/blob/main/eslint.config.js
warnings_fixed_justification: Both run inside npm run verify, which is the CI gate, so a warning stops a merge rather than being listed.
warnings_strict_justification: The linter is deliberately limited to correctness rather than style, so a failed lint means "this line will throw". Type checking gets stricter by construction: the number of type errors per file is written down and can only fall.
know_secure_design_justification: The app writes into another program folder and installs files written by strangers, so the design is built around least privilege and not trusting input. The renderer has no Node integration, no file access and no network beyond an explicit bridge. Every archive comes through one door that refuses paths climbing out of their folder, refuses names Windows treats specially, and caps sizes and ratios. Every write to the game folder is one transaction that rolls back whole. The catalog is signed with a pinned key, each archive is checked against a published SHA-256, and the project own remote switches are signed as well. Workflow tokens are read-only unless a job asks otherwise, and every action is pinned to a commit.
know_common_errors_justification: Path traversal (zip slip), time-of-check to time-of-use, unsafe zip expansion and trusting a file because of its name are the errors this kind of software gets wrong, and each has a guard and a test here. The project also keeps write-ups of what has gone wrong in docs/incidents/, each naming the test or check that would catch it again, and a test fails when one of those guards is renamed or deleted: https://github.com/dota2modmanager/dota2-mod-manager/tree/main/docs/incidents
crypto_published_justification: SHA-256 and Ed25519 from Node own crypto, and TLS from the platform. Nothing cryptographic is implemented in this project.
crypto_floss_justification: Node.js and its crypto are FLOSS.
crypto_working_justification: Integrity is SHA-256 and signatures are Ed25519. SHA-1 appears only where it is not a security mechanism: cache file names, and the fingerprint of a VPK own index, which the game format defines.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: No broken or weakened algorithm decides whether anything is trusted.
crypto_pfs_justification: Every connection is TLS provided by Node and Chromium, which negotiate ECDHE.
crypto_password_storage_justification: The app stores no passwords. Signing in with Discord uses the implicit grant in the user own browser; the token is used once to read the account name and is then dropped.
delivery_mitm_justification: Downloads and updates are HTTPS, from GitHub releases or the project own CDN.
delivery_unsigned_justification: Every release carries SHA256SUMS, a Sigstore attestation of that list produced by the release workflow, and an SBOM. Updates are verified by electron-updater against the hashes in the signed update feed. Mod archives are checked against mod-hashes.json, which the catalog publishes and signs with a key pinned in the app.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: No known vulnerability is open. npm audit runs over both lockfiles every morning and its findings appear in the project status issue the same day; Dependabot opens security updates and minor ones merge themselves once every check passes.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: The two high-severity code scanning findings of September 2026 were fixed the day they were reported, each with a test.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: Secret scanning and push protection are on. Every secret a workflow reads is listed in .github/credentials.json and tried against its own service every morning, and a test refuses a secret that is listed without a check: https://github.com/dota2modmanager/dota2-mod-manager/blob/main/.github/credentials.json
static_analysis_justification: CodeQL on every pull request, every push to main and weekly, plus ESLint and tsc --checkJs in the gate: https://github.com/dota2modmanager/dota2-mod-manager/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL security queries for JavaScript and TypeScript.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: Two high-severity findings were open in September 2026 and both were fixed the day they were reported, each with a test. Since 17 September the branch rule on main refuses to merge a pull request that adds an alert at High or higher, so a finding cannot reach main and wait.
static_analysis_often_justification: Every pull request, every push to main, and weekly.
dynamic_analysis_justification: Three kinds. The built installer and AppImage are installed and clicked through on Linux and Windows before a release becomes public: install a mod, switch it off, restart, switch it on, remove it, with the game folder checked on disk after every step. The VPK and zip parsers are fuzzed with seeded random input, and every input that broke one is kept as a test. A weekly mutation run breaks the promises the tests guard, to check the suite notices: https://github.com/dota2modmanager/dota2-mod-manager/blob/main/.github/workflows/e2e.yml
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: The project own code is JavaScript. No C or C++ is written here.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: The test suite is assertions, and the app refuses rather than assumes at every boundary that matters. Production builds carry those refusals but no extra assertions, so this is answered as unmet rather than claimed.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: Nothing of medium severity or above has been found by the dynamic runs. What the fuzzers found (a crash on a damaged VPK tree) was fixed and kept as a test.
achieve_passing_justification: The passing badge was awarded on 2026-09-20: https://www.bestpractices.dev/en/projects/14721
dco_justification: There is no DCO sign-off and no CLA. CONTRIBUTING.md states the inbound licence instead: opening a pull request means the change ships under GPL-3.0 as part of this program. With one maintainer and a handful of outside changes a year, a sign-off gate would turn away more contributions than it would protect: https://github.com/dota2modmanager/dota2-mod-manager/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
governance_justification: GOVERNANCE.md describes the model: one maintainer decides, in public, through pull requests; a second maintainer approves every change before it merges; the same checks gate everybody; and decisions that shape the project are recorded in DECISIONS.md with their reason: https://github.com/dota2modmanager/dota2-mod-manager/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md
code_of_conduct_justification: CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md in the repository root, in the standard location GitHub reads: https://github.com/dota2modmanager/dota2-mod-manager/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md
roles_responsibilities_justification: GOVERNANCE.md names the roles and what each one is responsible for: the maintainer, who reviews, releases, answers security reports and holds the keys outside GitHub; the second maintainer, who co-owns the organization and reads changes when they choose to; contributors; and the catalog authors, who are a separate project: https://github.com/dota2modmanager/dota2-mod-manager/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md
access_continuity_justification: Since 2026-09-23 the repository belongs to the dota2modmanager organization, and both maintainers are its owners. Either of them can create and close issues, approve and merge changes, push the tag that starts a release and change the branch rule, without the other; CI builds, signs and publishes from the tag with no personal key. What one person still holds (the config/app.json signing key, the domain, the mirror bucket) is listed with what losing it costs in GOVERNANCE.md, section Continuity: https://github.com/dota2modmanager/dota2-mod-manager/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md
bus_factor_justification: Two people can merge and release since 2026-09-23, but one person still writes most of the code and knows how it keeps up with a game update. DECISIONS.md lists it as a known gap under "Two maintainers, and one of them holds the keys": https://github.com/dota2modmanager/dota2-mod-manager/blob/main/DECISIONS.md
documentation_roadmap_justification: ROADMAP.md covers what is next, what comes later and what this project will not do at all: no telemetry, no required account, no paid features, no macOS build, no hosting mods as ours, and nothing that changes how the game plays: https://github.com/dota2modmanager/dota2-mod-manager/blob/main/ROADMAP.md
documentation_architecture_justification: ARCHITECTURE.md describes how the app is put together, module by module, including what is trusted and where: https://github.com/dota2modmanager/dota2-mod-manager/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md
documentation_security_justification: SECURITY.md has a section, "What you can expect, and what you cannot", listing the promises the app makes and the ones it refuses to make, and docs/assurance-case.md carries the argument behind them: https://github.com/dota2modmanager/dota2-mod-manager/blob/main/SECURITY.md
documentation_quick_start_justification: The README has an Install section that gets a new user to a working install and a first mod, and the site carries the same as illustrated guides: https://github.com/dota2modmanager/dota2-mod-manager/blob/main/README.md
documentation_current_justification: The generated reference (docs/API.md) is rebuilt from the source and test/api-docs.test.js fails when the two disagree; test/docs-current.test.js and test/decisions.test.js hold the hand-written documents against the repository, so a document that names something no longer here fails the build rather than ageing quietly: https://github.com/dota2modmanager/dota2-mod-manager/blob/main/docs/API.md
documentation_achievements_justification: The OpenSSF Best Practices badge, silver since 2026-09-23, is linked from the front page of both READMEs, beside the Scorecard badge: https://github.com/dota2modmanager/dota2-mod-manager/blob/main/README.md
accessibility_best_practices_justificati: The window follows what is reasonable for a desktop app: roles and labels on the controls that are not plain buttons, visible focus outlines rather than focus removed, @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) honoured in the stylesheets, a UI scale from 70% to 160%, and the whole interface in two languages. No formal audit has been run, so this is what is done rather than a certificate: https://github.com/dota2modmanager/dota2-mod-manager/blob/main/renderer
internationalization_justification: The app ships in English and Russian, including the native dialogs and the release notes. tools/check-i18n.js walks every translated string and fails the build when one has no English twin, so a half-translated screen cannot merge: https://github.com/dota2modmanager/dota2-mod-manager/blob/main/tools/check-i18n.js
sites_password_security_justification: No site or service in this project stores a password. There is no account: signing in with Discord is optional, the access token is used once to read a name and an avatar and is never written down, and the site is static.
maintenance_or_update_justification: The app updates itself through electron-updater, and every published release stays downloadable on the releases page, so an older copy can be updated or reinstalled at any time. The upgrade path needs no steps from the user: https://github.com/dota2modmanager/dota2-mod-manager/blob/main/RELEASING.md
vulnerability_report_credit_justificatio: No vulnerability report has been resolved in the last 12 months, so there is nobody to credit yet. SECURITY.md says reporters are credited in the release notes unless they ask not to be: https://github.com/dota2modmanager/dota2-mod-manager/blob/main/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_response_process_justifica: SECURITY.md documents it: reports go to a private GitHub advisory, a first reply comes within 48 hours, the current release is the one that gets fixed, and what is in scope and what belongs to the catalog authors is stated: https://github.com/dota2modmanager/dota2-mod-manager/blob/main/SECURITY.md
coding_standards_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states the style the repository keeps, and eslint.config.js is the machine-readable half of it. The linter is deliberately about code that cannot run rather than about formatting, which is recorded as a decision with its reason: https://github.com/dota2modmanager/dota2-mod-manager/blob/main/eslint.config.js
coding_standards_enforced_justification: npm run verify runs eslint over the whole repository, the same gate runs in CI on every pull request, and a pre-commit hook refuses a commit that would break it.
build_standard_variables_justification: No native binaries are produced. The app is JavaScript; electron-builder packages it with the Electron runtime, and there is no compiler or linker to pass CC, CFLAGS or LDFLAGS to.
build_preserve_debug_justification: Nothing is compiled or stripped. The JavaScript that ships is the JavaScript in this repository, readable inside the package.
build_non_recursive_justification: There is no recursive build. Packaging is one electron-builder invocation over the whole project.
build_repeatable_justification: The app own code is JavaScript, used directly rather than compiled, so there is no generation step to repeat. What CI packages around it is an installer, which is not bit-for-bit reproducible; the answer to "did this file come from this source" is a Sigstore provenance attestation over every file in SHA256SUMS rather than a reproduction: https://github.com/dota2modmanager/dota2-mod-manager/blob/main/SECURITY.md
installation_common_justification: Windows gets an NSIS installer that appears in Add or Remove Programs, and a portable build that needs no installation. Linux gets an AppImage. Uninstalling is the same conventional route and the app asks what should go with it: https://github.com/dota2modmanager/dota2-mod-manager/blob/main/README.md
installation_standard_variables_justific: There is no POSIX-style installation step to honour DESTDIR or a prefix. The NSIS installer lets the user choose the folder and otherwise follows Windows conventions; the AppImage is a single file the user puts where they like.
installation_development_quick_justifica: git clone, npm install, npm start, and npm test run the app and its tests with two runtime dependencies and no build step. npm run sandbox:seed builds a throwaway Dota tree with real mods in it, so a developer never has to test against their own game: https://github.com/dota2modmanager/dota2-mod-manager/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
external_dependencies_justification: package.json lists them, and every release carries a CycloneDX SBOM of what the app actually ships as dota2-mod-manager.cdx.json: https://github.com/dota2modmanager/dota2-mod-manager/blob/main/package.json
dependency_monitoring_justification: Dependabot watches the npm dependencies and the pinned GitHub Actions and opens pull requests for both, npm audit runs in CI on every push, and a scheduled job reports anything outstanding into the pinned status issue: https://github.com/dota2modmanager/dota2-mod-manager/blob/main/.github/dependabot.yml
updateable_reused_components_justificati: The app ships two runtime dependencies, both from npm and neither vendored into this repository, so updating one is a version bump. Nothing is forked or copied in.
interfaces_current_justification: The runtime is kept current rather than pinned to an old line: Electron 44 and Node 24 today, with Dependabot opening the bumps. No deprecated Electron or Node API is knowingly used, and the type checker runs against the current typings with a ceiling that can only fall.
automated_integration_testing_justificat: Every push and every pull request runs the suite on Linux and on Windows, and a separate job installs the built AppImage and clicks through installing, switching and removing a mod against a real Dota tree. Each run reports pass or fail as a required check: https://github.com/dota2modmanager/dota2-mod-manager/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml
regression_tests_added50_justification: Well above half: a fix carries a test or a line in the commit saying why it does not, and tools/pr-test-rule.mjs fails the pull request when neither is there. Incidents get a named guard of their own, held together by test/incidents.test.js: https://github.com/dota2modmanager/dota2-mod-manager/blob/main/tools/pr-test-rule.mjs
test_statement_coverage80_justification: Statement coverage is above 92% of lines, measured on Linux and on Windows by node --test --experimental-test-coverage, and the gate refuses anything under 90%: https://github.com/dota2modmanager/dota2-mod-manager/blob/main/.github/coverage-baseline.json
test_policy_mandated_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states it as a rule, and tools/pr-test-rule.mjs enforces it on every pull request: new behaviour arrives with a test, or the commit says No-Test-Because and why: https://github.com/dota2modmanager/dota2-mod-manager/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
implement_secure_design_justification: docs/assurance-case.md sets out the principles this app is built on and where each one lives: least privilege in the renderer, one door for every dangerous thing, failing in the direction that costs least on purpose, never running code fetched from the network, and checks that do not depend on one another: https://github.com/dota2modmanager/dota2-mod-manager/blob/main/docs/assurance-case.md
crypto_algorithm_agility_justification: Deliberately not agile. The app verifies ed25519 signatures against keys pinned in its own source and checks archives against sha256 from a signed list. Accepting a negotiated algorithm would mean accepting a weaker one chosen by whoever is on the other end; changing either algorithm is a release, which is the point.
crypto_credential_agility_justification: The app stores no authentication credential and no private key. Signing in with Discord uses the token once to read a name and an avatar and then discards it; what is kept is an id, a name and a picture, in the ordinary settings file.
crypto_used_network_justification: Every address the app contacts is https, and the list of them is published in PRIVACY.md. Nothing falls back to plain http: https://github.com/dota2modmanager/dota2-mod-manager/blob/main/PRIVACY.md
crypto_tls12_justification: TLS is whatever Node and Electron negotiate, which is 1.2 at the oldest and 1.3 in practice. The app never lowers the default or disables a protocol check.
crypto_certificate_verification_justific: Certificate verification is the platform default and is never switched off. There is no rejectUnauthorized: false and no NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED anywhere in this repository.
crypto_verification_private_justificatio: The app sends no credential and no private information in a header at all. Where it does use TLS, verification is the default and is not disabled.
signed_releases_justification: Every release carries SHA256SUMS and a Sigstore provenance attestation over that list, signed by the release workflow at the tagged commit, so gh attestation verify ties a downloaded file to a commit in this repository. The keys are Sigstore short-lived certificates rather than a private key sitting where the files are served. SECURITY.md documents the commands: https://github.com/dota2modmanager/dota2-mod-manager/blob/main/SECURITY.md
version_tags_signed_justification: Tags are not signed. The release artifacts are attested through Sigstore instead, which is what a user actually downloads and can check; signing the tags as well is worth doing and has not been set up.
input_validation_justification: Everything from outside is checked before it is used: a name inside an archive is a name and never a path, foreign zips come through one reader that refuses traversal, links and sizes beyond their budget, catalog records are validated before they become library entries, and guide HTML goes through an allowlist of tags. docs/assurance-case.md walks each of them: https://github.com/dota2modmanager/dota2-mod-manager/blob/main/docs/assurance-case.md
hardening_justification: The window runs with context isolation on, node integration off, and a content security policy that admits no remote script. The app asks for no elevation, downloads no code, and writes only in its own data folder and the game folder.
assurance_case_justification: docs/assurance-case.md: what is being protected, the five trust boundaries and where each is enforced, the threats one at a time with what answers them, the secure design principles applied, and what the case does not claim. Every answer ends with the test that would fail if it stopped being true: https://github.com/dota2modmanager/dota2-mod-manager/blob/main/docs/assurance-case.md
